newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian court halts Purneftegaz ownership change.
newsitem.headline: Russian court halts Purneftegaz ownership change.

text.p: A Russian appeals court, in the latest twist in a tug-of-war between Russian oil groups SIDANKO and Rosneft for ownership of oil producer Purneftegaz, has suspended an earlier ruling awarding the company to SIDANKO, a Rosneft spokesman said on Wednesday.

Vladimir Vyunitsky, press secretary of Rosneft president Yuri Bespalov, told Reuters the Supreme Arbitration Court had decided on July 14 to examine an appeal by OAO NK Rosneft against a ruling on July 3 by the Moscow Region Arbitration Court awarding a controlling stake in Purneftegaz to SIDANKO.
He did not say when the appeal would be heard.

Purneftegaz produced 169,600 barrels of oil per day in 1996. U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers estimates its reserves at 800 million tonnes (5.6 billion barrels), against Russia's total reserves of 49 billion barrels.
The producer would be a valuable gain for SIDANKO, which produced 20.81 million tonnes (416,200 bpd) in 1996.
Its loss would be a body blow for Rosneft, a state oil holding company undergoing privatisation, which altogether produced 13.10 million tonnes (262,000 bpd) in 1996.

The government transferred OAO Purneftegaz to Rosneft in January 1995 as part of a restructuring of the oil industry, having originally allocated it to SIDANKO. Several courts have since confirmed Rosneft's ownership.

OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (SIDANKO) had already lodged another appeal about Purneftegaz with the Supreme Arbitration Court in March of this year, but that has not yet been heard.
Both parties can appeal the court's rulings to the court's presidium, but there would not be any further avenues of appeal after that.
